In the next 7-8 weeks, Saudi Aramco would be able to boost capacity by 1.2m b/d using an existing natural gas pipe, making changes to ship crude. Riyadh didn't disclose further details, other than the line would need to revert to nat gas by May as the kingdom needs it to feed power stations during the summer months.

The pipeline was seized by the Saudis after Saddam Hussein invaded Kuwait in Aug 1990 and later it was repurposed for use in the country's Master Gas System]

More long-term, Saudi officials said they plan to boost shipping capacity of the East-West pipeline to ~10m b/d in the next 2-3 years, mostly improving pumping capacity (rather than building another pipe).

Powerful quantum computers could pose a serious risk.

And preparing the world's infrastructure for quantum attacks will take longer than most people expect.

I came across this breakdown from @PaloAltoNtwks, and it got me thinking about how many systems we'd actually need to upgrade.

We're talking about:

→ Payment systems
→ Digital identities and authentication
→ Software updates and security checks
→ Older connected devices that may be difficult to update

With so much infrastructure to upgrade, I can see why NIST isn't waiting around. It finalized its first three quantum-resistant cryptography standards in 2024 and is already urging organizations to adopt them.

There's another concern, too.

Encrypted data stolen today could become readable years later, once quantum computers become powerful enough.

Lots of ground to cover, so best start early if you ask me.

New week. Inflation in focus. Nuclear investment gathering momentum.

🔩 COPPER
LME copper traded above $14,600/t this morning as Chinese infrastructure stimulus hopes met fresh supply concerns in Chile. Centinela strike action and potential disruption at Escondida put mine supply firmly on this week’s watchlist.

🥇 GOLD
Gold around $4,171 after retreating from an early one-week high. The dollar is keeping pressure on bullion ahead of CPI Wednesday, followed by PPI and retail sales Thursday.

📌 WEEK AHEAD
Inflation data, the dollar, Chilean mine developments and follow-through in uranium equities.
TSX and TSXV are closed today for Canadian Thanksgiving, so Canadian mining stocks rejoin the action Tuesday.

My focus: how the metals respond to the data—and whether miners confirm the move. ⚒️

The supply overhang that crushed alts has dissipated and is, for the first time in the asset class's history, manageable.

Payouts to holders minus new supply, as a share of market value:
2021-22: -17% a year
2026: -2.9%

Tokens paying holders more than they dilute them: 4% then, 17% now.

Part of this is capital discipline. Better unlock management, maturing protocols, and revenue-funded buybacks. Tokens are starting to take on equity-like properties.

The other part is demand. It's showing up. Tokenisation first, and eventually AI agentic commerce.

Less drag, more demand. Structurally, crypto has never been in better shape.

@RealVision

One of my more controversial bets: the AI feed will be the form factor of 2027!

Most people don’t know what to prompt, and they won’t prompt their way into complicated agentic workflows. With chat, we ask users for digital labor: figure out what AI can do, explain the task, provide the context, repeat. That’s a lot to ask if we want billions of people using agents every day. 

Meanwhile, people already spend hours in feeds. Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn. They know how to scroll, discover something useful, and act on it.

An intelligent system that knows you should bring you the next useful action. Here’s the email you need to answer, already drafted. Here are the latest sales numbers, with an update ready to send to your team. You approve, edit, dismiss, or jump into chat to go deeper. That’s how people will discover what agents can do, without having to invent a prompt first.

And you can put ads in a feed, one of the biggest business models on the internet. A system that understands your plans can recommend a relevant restaurant, product, or service, clearly labeled as sponsored. You get a reason to come back every day, useful work ready to approve, and a business model to fund the agents doing it.
